Passwords, recovery tokens and file inputs are never persisted in drafts.
Successful submissions clear the corresponding draft while failed submissions retain it for recovery.
Phone values remain canonical local Iranian mobile numbers matching ^09\d{9}$; the backend is authoritative.
Locale is persisted locally for continuity, applied to the document language and direction, and synchronized to the authenticated profile when changed.

Required form controls show a persistent red asterisk beside their labels; custom form-level validation prevents the browser's default empty-field bubble, marks missing controls and clears the error state when the user edits the field.
Desktop hero spacing is controlled by a responsive flex gap and component margins are normalized to avoid uneven stacking.
The login marketing panel uses a brand-neutral, low-contrast HSE workplace photo with a readability overlay; the previous CSS illustration is removed from the login hero.
The standalone login hero icon is removed so the locale-specific wordmark is the only logo inside the desktop hero brand panel.
The login brand panel uses the supplied flex, spacing, border, translucent background, shadow and blur declarations without an added fixed width.

The login approvals content was replaced rather than duplicated: a semantic support bar renders the requested Persian/English support statement and the supplied Qazvin Science and Technology Park logo at compact icon size; the old approvals strings and icon list are no longer rendered.

The localized login hero heading keeps its existing content and RTL/LTR behavior while using a reduced responsive font scale, tighter line-height and the available hero measure so it remains on one line at supported desktop sizes without clipping.

The localized login brand panel is the sole content of the toolbar brand container; the intermediate role/workspace chooser is removed from the login flow and successful credentials navigate directly to the panel.

The desktop hero uses a 16px top offset plus the requested 25px brand-panel top margin, keeps the login/register CTA row in normal flow while visibly lowering it by 10–20px with a responsive transform, gives the feature list the requested 25px bottom margin and lifts it an additional 10–20px with a responsive transform, keeps the login-card logo physically left-aligned in both locales through direction-specific flex alignment, grows to fill the available panel height, distributes groups with space-between and larger responsive gaps, restores the shield/chart/hardhat safety illustration between the CTAs and features, lets the illustration container show the marketing panel background through a transparent surface, and removes unavailable website/contact destinations from the login toolbar.
Registration step one retains the account-type title and guidance, while later detail/review steps omit the requested redundant account-creation heading and automatic-draft description.

The /admin route is separated from regular user navigation and selects a distinct SUPER_ADMIN global workspace or ORG_ADMIN organization workspace; global user controls remain behind a SUPER_ADMIN-only /admin/* API boundary, while organization member controls remain tenant-scoped through the existing /members API. Global role changes and deactivation revoke active sessions, and the last active SUPER_ADMIN cannot be removed.

AI provider selection is role-specific: risk requests resolve AI_RISK_PROVIDER/AI_RISK_MODEL with AI_RISK_FALLBACK_PROVIDER/AI_RISK_FALLBACK_MODEL failover, chat resolves AI_CHAT_PROVIDER/AI_CHAT_MODEL and bounded same-user conversation history plus tenant-scoped knowledge, and ArvanCloud AI credentials remain server-only in ignored local environment files.

AI usage is recorded only from validated provider-reported counts, linked to the initiating user, organization and source request/message, and exposed through a role-checked aggregate endpoint without prompts, completions or credentials.

FMEA process suggestions combine active global or organization-scoped JobCatalog relationships with the configured server-side risk provider; database and AI results remain suggestions until the user explicitly selects or adds each item, and all AI prompt/output fields are bounded and sanitized.

Risk AI uses GPT-5-Mini as the primary model, retries bounded transient failures, then uses the configured ArvanCloud AI GPT-5-Mini route through the server-side credential before using the deterministic knowledge fallback.

Risk-row AI responses include bounded advisory integer S/O/D suggestions with rationale; the frontend renders them after the score panel and requires explicit apply or dismiss, while applying updates controlled scores and live RPN only and never persists the suggestion automatically.

New FMEA process fields are backward-compatible nullable database columns for existing rows, while the create API requires a bounded activity description and validates organization/project/catalog ownership before persistence.

Password values use a dedicated LTR text flow with the same leading inset as the email field while the visibility control retains its end-side placement; the login placeholder is localized through the shared translation dictionaries.

The current working-tree release is deployed to the authorized Windows server behind https://app.nivasafe.com using PM2 for API supervision, a Windows startup task for pm2 resurrect, and the existing Nginx reverse-proxy arrangement; the prior release and runtime environment were retained for rollback.

Production frontend API selection is based on Vite's production build mode rather than the repository development NODE_ENV value, so the deployed bundle uses the same-origin /api/v1 proxy and cannot fall back to localhost:5044.

The production API database connection was repaired by provisioning a dedicated database-scoped application account with a generated secret and updating the server-only DATABASE_URL; login throttling remains enabled with LOGIN_RATE_LIMIT_MAX=60 and a 15-minute window rather than being disabled, and Fastify trusts forwarded client IPs only from loopback Nginx.
The app sidebar intentionally retains its icon and workspace context but removes the side-brand-wordmark element from all panel layouts at the user's request.

The new-assessment type selector keeps single-click selection and explicit keyboard/button continuation, supports double-click continuation for both FMEA and RULA cards, and no longer renders the dashboard shortcut.

The /choose-path selector writes the confirmed FMEA/RULA path to sessionStorage before navigation; localStorage is used only as a fallback default, while FMEA and RULA provide a route-safe change-method link back to the selector. Its visible stepper has exactly three stages—assessment type, assessment details and review/confirmation—with assessment type as stage 1; the former basic-information item is not rendered.

The FMEA creation stepper keeps the existing form fields and review content, uses explicit process-information and review/register states, stores the current draft step in sessionStorage, guards the registration request against duplicate clicks, and uses the server-created assessment ID to enter the existing report route as the report/results stage.

The FMEA assessment-information grid overrides the shared bottom alignment so the code and scope labels and inputs start at the same vertical position; the code hint remains in the code field flow and the two-column row stacks responsively.

Registration owns the initial workspace bootstrap on the server: user, organization, membership, audit event and localized DEFAULT project are committed in one Prisma transaction; the frontend uses the organization returned by the subsequent login and does not issue a duplicate project request.

Project-list reads use an idempotent organization-scoped DEFAULT project upsert to backfill older workspaces and restore soft-deleted starters without creating a shared cross-organization record or changing existing project content; the project route rejects deletion of the reserved starter.
The assistant route keeps its existing path and behavior while the panel navigation label uses explicit AI-chat wording: گفتگو با هوش مصنوعی / Chat with AI.

Administrator additions use the existing email invitation and acceptance flow. ASSISTANT is organization-scoped with bounded operational permissions; ORG_ADMIN can manage organization roles, while only SUPER_ADMIN can invite or assign SUPER_ADMIN.

Route transitions use a single accessible branded loader mounted inside BrowserRouter; the loader settles after a short bounded interval, avoids blocking pointer input, and disables decorative animation when prefers-reduced-motion is enabled.

The FMEA register is server-authoritative for S/O/D validation, RPN and risk-level recalculation; row edits/deletes are tenant-scoped and audit-recorded, while Word output is generated as escaped Office Open XML DOCX and the legacy .doc route remains a compatibility alias.

The FMEA report is a tenant-scoped read model derived from persisted assessment rows and actions; report save records the current version in the audit log, suggestions remain unpersisted until explicit registration, and corrective actions may link to an FMEA row with ON DELETE SET NULL preservation.

RULA activity measurements use bounded explicit units, posture images are uploaded only after assessment creation through a tenant-validated image route, and AI posture-image generation is reserved as a documented future extension rather than a fake current integration.

RULA posture observations are stored as validated nullable analysis JSON; the server derives authoritative scoring inputs from edited observations, while the current image skeleton is an explicit future-model extension and never claims live AI detection.

RULA result reports are derived from tenant-scoped posture observations; corrective actions store bounded rulaImpact metadata, and predicted scores are labeled as non-definitive estimates rather than reassessment results.

The production login-specific rate-limit window remains enabled for brute-force protection, while local development omits that route-specific countdown and retains the application-wide abuse limiter so test users are not blocked by the production login timer.

Registration always starts with a visible personal/organization selector while preserving non-sensitive draft fields; login persists the first server-authorized organization returned by the API and enters the panel directly, while the existing in-panel company switcher remains available.

Dashboard layout state is intentionally browser-scoped by authenticated user and active organization because the request is limited to dashboard UX/personalization; widget removal is reversible and never deletes business data, while sidebar collapse state remains local to the browser.
The Windows production API is explicitly bound to 127.0.0.1:5044 through HOST and PM2; the direct public firewall rule is disabled so Nginx is the only public API ingress.

The canonical public web address is https://app.nivasafe.com. HTTP and HTTPS legacy web aliases redirect with 301 to that address, while API aliases remain on https://api.nivasafe.com for API compatibility.

PWA service-worker registration disables the browser worker cache, checks for releases on registration, visibility, page show and reconnection, and performs a bounded periodic check; normal waiting workers are activated only after explicit user action and the controlled page reloads once, while the one-time v12 migration claims and navigates stale open windows

Registration contact fields use one shared classifier for email versus phone input; the API revalidates normalized values, rejects unknown payload keys and incomplete organization details, and applies the reserved/allowed display-name policy before persistence

Multi-company creation is available to authenticated users and atomically adds an ORG_ADMIN membership plus a localized DEFAULT project; selected organization IDs are membership-checked in the client and re-authorized by the backend on every scoped request

Each organization stores its own subscription plan, provider, status, expiry and external reference; production-created companies remain PENDING_PAYMENT until their own payment succeeds, and local checkout simulation is development-only

Company switching routes users with inactive or unpaid subscriptions to the organization billing surface; the organization page does not request operational dashboard data until the selected company is active and its subscription is usable
